questions.q: Who plays Black Adam in the 2022 DC film of the same name?
questions.why: Dwayne Johnson stars as Teth-Adam in the 2022 film, a spin-off from Shazam! that was pushed by Johnson for years.

questions.q: What is Black Adam's original name before he gains his powers?
questions.why: He starts out as an ancient man called Teth-Adam, chosen by the wizard Shazam as his champion, before he is corrupted.

questions.q: In which year did Black Adam first appear, in Fawcett Comics' The Marvel Family #1?
questions.why: Black Adam debuted in The Marvel Family #1 in 1945, from Fawcett, and DC revived him in the 1970s after acquiring the characters.

options: Geoff Johns and David S. Goyer
Otto Binder and C. C. Beck
questions.why: Writer Otto Binder and artist C. C. Beck created him for Fawcett; Johns and Goyer only reworked him in the 2000s.

questions.q: In Jerry Ordway's 1994 revised comic origin, Teth-Adam is the son of which pharaoh?
questions.why: The Power of Shazam! retold his origin as a son of Ramesses II, born in the 13th century BC.

questions.q: In the 1970s revival comics, which Egyptian god gives Black Adam his stamina?
questions.why: Shazam! #28 lists Shu for stamina, with other gods giving strength, power, wisdom, speed and courage.

questions.q: Black Adam is a famous archenemy of which hero and the Marvel Family?
questions.why: Sivana and Mister Mind, along with Black Adam, rank among Shazam's best-known enemies.

questions.q: Black Adam rules and defends which fictional Middle Eastern nation in the comics?
questions.why: In modern comics, he is the champion of Kahndaq, a fictional country on the Sinai Peninsula, which he fiercely protects.

questions.q: In 52, Black Adam's wife Adrianna Tomaz is transformed by a magic amulet into which hero?
questions.why: Adam used the amulet to turn Adrianna into the superheroine Isis, and the couple married with the Marvel Family attending.

questions.q: Who directed the 2022 film Black Adam?
questions.why: Jaume Collet-Serra directed the film; its screenplay credits go to Adam Sztykiel, Rory Haines and Sohrab Noshirvani.
